```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>"

```

```{r setup, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE  }
library(seabORD)
```

This example assumes that the model has already been calibrated. If not, follow the calibration article first and then return to this example.

# Introduction & background

Now that we have run our calibration step and discerned the prey values resulting in moderate conditions in the absence of wind farms, we can continue with running the main SeabORD runs with matched pairs of baseline (no ORDs) and scenario (ORDs included).

# This example

In this example we will run 1 scenario run (wind farm footprints included) with a prey value of 200.

## Prepare inputs

For further information on inputs, please see Article "Example kittiwake: step 1 - seabORD inputs".

This script will import the example parameters sets and spatial data, which are largely similar to the calibration inputs. Note will be given where these differ considerably, i.e., with regard to the inclusion of different wind farm footprints.

### Parameter sets

#### Par

NOTE: "NScalefactor" is **set to 1 meaning we are running with 100%** **of the population**, which is customary for scenario runs.

```{r}
Par_example <- seabORD::example_lists_dd$Par
str(Par_example)
```

#### modPar

```{r}
modPar_example <- seabORD::example_lists_dd$modPar
str(modPar_example)
```

Create the output folder , for example "output_seabORD_scenario" and assign it

```{r, eval=FALSE}
# set the output location in ModPar 
# This is just an example, you can place the output in any directory.
if (!dir.exists("./output_seabORD_scenario")) {
  dir.create("./output_seabORD_scenario")
}
```

```{r}
modPar_example$outputdir <- "output_seabORD_scenario"
```

We intend to run 5 replicates so need to change this in modPar.

```{r}
modPar_example$Nreplicates <- 1
```

#### Include the calibration in Par

NOTE: Run this test! here the replicates are specified - this must align with the number of prey values listed in "Par_example\$Pmedian"

```{r}
seabORD::check_calibration_inputs(
  Par = Par_example,
  modPar = modPar_example
)
```

Given calibarted values. Modify Par so that it reflects. You can use the built in function to do so.

Check the pre-set value, and change it based on the calibration values.

```{r}
str(Par_example$Pmedian)
```

Change it:

```{r}
# min prey value from range determined in calibration
Pmin <- 173  
# max prey value from range determined in calibration
Pmax <- 174

Par_example <- seabORD::create_prey_sequence_in_par(
  Par = Par_example,
  modPar = modPar_example,
  Pmin = Pmin,
  Pmax = Pmax
)


```

```{r}
str(Par_example$Pmedian) #should be good to go!
```

#### ordPar

```{r}
ordPar_example <-  seabORD::example_lists_dd$ordPar
str(ordPar_example) # Including wind farms Nearth na Goithe and Inch Cape
```

#### Switches

Turn on the switch "savebirdflightmap", to see an example of the birdflightmap output. Turn on "saverds" to save the outputs as rds.

```{r}
switches_example <- seabORD::example_lists_dd$switches
switches_example$savebirdflightmap <- TRUE
switches_example$saverds <- TRUE 

str(switches_example)
```

### Assorted spatial inputs

Now load in all the spatial inputs.

#### seamask

```{r}
seamask_example <- seabORD::get_example_seamask()
```

#### spadat1

```{r}
spadat1_example <- seabORD::get_example_spadat1("UK9002491")

# Overwite with the exact colony location of Whinnyfold used when creating map in step 1.1
whinnyfold_lon <- -1.85849
whinnyfold_lat <- 57.388807

spadat1_example$Longitude <- whinnyfold_lon
spadat1_example$Latitude  <- whinnyfold_lat
spadat1_example$flt.LONG  <- whinnyfold_lon
spadat1_example$flt.LAT   <- whinnyfold_lat
```

#### spadat2

```{r}
spadat2_example <- seabORD::get_example_spadat2("UK9002491")
```

#### spdat

```{r}
spdat_example  <- seabORD::get_spdat_example("KI")
```

#### BrdData

```{r}
BrdData_example_dd <- seabORD::get_example_brddata_dd()
```

#### FrgCompData

```{r}
FrgCompData_example_dd <- seabORD::get_example_frgcompdata_dd()
```

#### fltdist_base

```{r}
fltdist_base_example <- seabORD::get_example_fltdist_base_dd()
```

#### FlightGridcorrection

```{r}
FlightGridcorrection <- seabORD::FlightGridcorrection_3035


```

#### ORDpoly

```{r}
ORDpoly_example <- seabORD::ORDpoly_example_wfold
```

You can plot the ORD footprints:

```{r}
seabORD::plot_ORDpoly(
    ORDpoly = ORDpoly_example,
    caption = "data ORDpoly run decay"
)
```

# Running seabORD

Now that all the inputs are ready we can run the model using. SeabORD runs including wind farms and full populations can take a while to run - even with a relatively small population of \~ 3,000 pairs.

The output will be saved in in your output directory set up in modPar.

To learn more about the main functions behind seabORD you can read the article on the main functions

To see how you can read in and plot the results you can read the article "Example kittiwake: step 4 - interpreting the outputs" where we have an example output for you to play with.

```{r,  eval = FALSE}
SeabORDoutput <- seabord(Par = Par_example,
                         ordPar = ordPar_example,
                         modPar = modPar_example,
                         switches = switches_example,
                         seamask = seamask_example,
                         spadat1 = spadat1_example,
                         spadat2 = spadat2_example,
                         spdat = spdat_example,
                         BrdData = BrdData_example,
                         FrgCompData = FrgCompData_example,
                         fltdist_base = fltdist_base_example,
                         FlightGridcorrection = FlightGridcorrection,
                         ORDpoly = ORDpoly_example)

# Save SeabORDsummary:
 if (switches_example$saverds) {
    saveRDS("SeabORDoutput",
            file.path(modPar_example$outputdir,
                      paste0("sb_out_", gsub("\\.", "_", make.names(paste0(modPar_example$reference,"_", Sys.Date()))),".rds")))
}
```
